successors.note: 'Theodosius gains Western Empire' (Frigidus infobox); he died four months later and the roman-empire row ends in 394, the western-roman-empire row starts in 395.

capitals.name: Lugdunum (Lyon)
capitals.note: Named only as 'Lyons', where Eugenius was proclaimed on 22 August 392; the page names no capital.

capitals.name: Mediolanum (Milan)
capitals.note: Mentioned because Bishop Ambrose left his see at Milan when Eugenius's court arrived; the page names no capital and gives no year for the arrival (after the 393 march into Italy).

rulers.name: Eugenius
rulers.title: usurper Augustus of the West
rulers.note: Infobox 'Reign: 22 August 392 - 6 September 394'; set up by the Frankish magister militum Arbogast; beheaded after the Frigidus.

correction.text: Gaul as the Roman Empire held it in 392: Eugenius was 'elevated to augustus on 22 August 392 at Lyons'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the page names only Lyons, the place of the proclamation on 22 August 392. Gaul is the researcher's reading; the page mentions the Rhine frontier and alliances with the Alamanni and Franks. No Spain, no Africa on either page. No area.

correction.text: Gaul and Italy, the West that Eugenius and Arbogast held after they marched 'into Italy in the spring of 393'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Eugenius and Arbogast marched into 'Italy in the spring of 393' (Eugenius page); Theodosius had proclaimed Honorius Augustus of the West in January 393. Spain and Africa are not mentioned on either page and are not drawn; the Frigidus article has the battle on 'the eastern border of Roman Italy'. No area.

region.text: Gaul as the Roman Empire held it in 392: Eugenius was 'elevated to augustus on 22 August 392 at Lyons'

ledger.note: 22 August 392: Arbogast raises Eugenius to Augustus of the West at Lyons. 'Eugenius was elevated to augustus on 22 August 392 at Lyons, by Arbogast'; infobox 'Reign: 22 August 392 - 6 September 394'. The page does not say which provinces recognised him; Gaul is the researcher's reading.

region.text: Italy, entered by Eugenius and Arbogast in the spring of 393

ledger.note: spring 393: Eugenius and Arbogast march into Italy. They marched into 'Italy in the spring of 393'; the page notes Theodosius promoted Honorius to Augustus of the West in January 393, which 'signaled that Theodosius considered Eugenius's rule illegitimate'. The page does not say Italy had been under Valentinian II's court at Milan; the Frigidus article has Eugenius as a 'rebel augustus in the eastern border of Roman Italy'.

region.text: the Frigidus battlefield 'near the Julian Alps', on 'the eastern border of Roman Italy'

ledger.note: 5 September 394: Theodosius reaches the Julian Alps. The battle was 'fought on 5 and 6 September 394' near the Julian Alps 'through which Theodosius's army had passed'; the passes' 'eastern ends ... were undefended'.

region.text: the Frigidus battlefield 'near the Julian Alps', on 'the eastern border of Roman Italy'

ledger.note: 6 September 394: the Frigidus is won. Eugenius 'was beheaded' after his pleas for mercy went unanswered; Arbogast 'committed suicide'. The Eugenius page has Eugenius dying on 6 September 394 and Arbogast's suicide 'the next day'.

region.text: Gaul and Italy, the West that Eugenius and Arbogast held after they marched 'into Italy in the spring of 393'

ledger.note: 6 September 394: the usurpation ends and Theodosius holds the whole empire. Frigidus infobox: 'Theodosian victory', 'Theodosius gains Western Empire'; 'A mere four months later he died', leaving Honorius and Arcadius in charge.

wars.name: Battle of the Frigidus

zones.text: the Frigidus battlefield 'near the Julian Alps', on 'the eastern border of Roman Italy'

wars.outcome: Theodosian victory: the usurper Eugenius was beheaded and the general Arbogast committed suicide on 6-7 September 394; Theodosius gained the Western Empire.
wars.note: The page dates the battle 5 and 6 September 394 and describes it as the end of a war that began when Arbogast raised Eugenius on 22 August 392.

certainty.note: The pages name Lyons, Italy and the Julian Alps only; no province list is given for Eugenius's regime.

sources.title: Eugenius

notes: A rebel state Cliopatria lacks, named by the roman-empire dossier ('Eugenius (usurper)', contest 392-394). Two pages opened. Neither gives the provinces Eugenius held; Gaul (Lyons) and Italy (393) are the only lands the pages support, Spain and Africa are not mentioned and are not drawn. The roman-empire dossier's contest zone is the researcher's reading too. Wikidata id unknown. Gazetteer: 'Julian Alps' and the Frigidus (Vipava) are not names.
